proofs.proof_tex:
Because the assertion is existential, choose admissible fixed constants with \(q=5\), \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\), and \(C\) large enough to dominate all of the bounded quantities below.  Put \(n_{\mathcal R}=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(n_{\mathcal E}=n-n_{\mathcal R}\), and complete the finitely many initial rows in any way satisfying the same strict inequalities.  Write \(M_n=\max\{1,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\}\) and fix numbers \(a_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1>0\), all sufficiently small relative to \(C\).

We first give an anchor-exact law.  Conditional on \(R=1\), let \(X\) have density one half on each of \([-2,-1]\) and \([1,2]\), let \(A\) be an independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) variable, and let \(E_a\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), be independent centered Rademacher variables taking values \(\pm\sigma_a\).  If \(X=1+u\), \(0\leq u\leq1\), set
\[
 \Delta_n(u)=a_0\cos(2\pi M_nu),\qquad
 Y(a)=1+u-\Delta_n(u)+E_a,
\]
and if \(X=-1-u\), set \(Y(a)=-1-u+E_a\).  Conditional on \(R=0\), let \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), put \(X=1+U\), \(A=0\), and \(Y(0)=Y(1)=Y=1+U\).  Finally take \(V\) uniform and independent of all the preceding variables.  Consistency then holds by construction and trial randomization holds because \(A\) is independent of \((X,Y(0),Y(1))\).

Use the genuine squared outcome-regression loss
\[
 L((x,y);\theta)=\{y-\mu_0(x;\theta)\}^2,
 \qquad \mu_0(x;\theta)=\theta,
 \qquad \Theta=\mathbb R.
 \tag{1}
\]
Since \(M_n\) is an integer, \(\int_0^1\Delta_n(u)\,du=0\).  The two covariate components have opposite means, so
\[
 E_{P_n}(Y\mid R=1,A=0)
 =\frac12\int_0^1(1+u-\Delta_n(u))\,du
  +\frac12\int_0^1(-1-u)\,du=0.
\]
Consequently the risk in (1) has the unique interior minimizer \(\theta_n=0\), its Hessian is \(H_n=2\), and the score equation in \(\mathrm{ass:score\text{-}equation}\) holds.  For an external point \(z=(1+u,1+u,v)\), the displayed definition of \(s_n\) gives
\[
 s_n(z)=2E_{P_n}(|Y|\mid R=1,A=0)(1+u).
 \tag{2}
\]
The factor in front of \(1+u\) is bounded above and away from zero: the negative covariate component alone gives a uniform positive lower bound when \(a_0,\sigma_0\) are chosen small.  Thus the conditional law of \(s_n(Z)\) given \(R=0\) has a density bounded uniformly in \(n\), which proves \(\mathrm{ass:score\text{-}margin}\).

The empirical minimizer in the frozen construction is the trial-control sample mean \(\widehat\theta_n\), and \(\widehat H_n=2\).  Conditional on a nonempty trial-control sample,
\[
 \widehat s_n(1+u,1+u,v)
 =2\left\{n_{\mathcal R,0}^{-1}
   \sum_{i\leq n_{\mathcal R}:A_i=0}|Y_i-\widehat\theta_n|\right\}
   |1+u-\widehat\theta_n|.
 \tag{3}
\]
Bounded second moments, the fixed-stratum sampling assumption, and Chebyshev's inequality give \(\widehat\theta_n=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\), while the probability of an empty control arm tends to zero.  On the event \(|\widehat\theta_n|<1/2\), the last factor in (3) is \(1+u-\widehat\theta_n\), a strictly increasing function of \(u\).  Hence, with probability tending to one, the generated ranks are exactly the ordinary ranks of the continuous variable \(U\); the label \(V\) is never used.

We next verify the local-bias restriction rather than assume it.  For a population prefix fraction \(v=k/n_{\mathcal E}\), let
\[
 \pi_n^+=\frac{\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}/2}
 {\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}/2+\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}},
 \qquad
 B_n=\frac{1-\pi_n^+}{1-\pi_n^+/2}.
\]
On the retained part \(0\leq u\leq v\) of the positive component, the trial conditional mean is \(1+u-\Delta_n(u)\), the external mean is \(1+u\), and direct conditioning in the definition of \(m_{n,k,0}\) yields
\[
 m_{n,k,0}(1+u)
 =1+u-\Delta_n(u)+B_n\Delta_n(u).
 \tag{4}
\]
Outside that part, \(m_{n,k,0}=m_{n,k,1}\).  Taking the conditional expectation of the displayed \(\eta_{n,k}\), both residual terms vanish by the definitions of \(m_{n,k,a}\); therefore
\[
 b_{n,k}=T_{n,k}-\tau_n
 =E_{P_n}\{m_{n,k,1}(X)-m_{n,k,0}(X)\mid R=1\}
 =-\frac{B_n}{2}\int_0^v\Delta_n(u)\,du.
 \tag{5}
\]
Here \(\tau_n=0\), because the two potential outcomes have the same conditional mean.  Since \(0\leq B_n\leq1\),
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\sqrt n\,b_{n,k}|
 \leq \frac{a_0\sqrt n}{4\pi M_n}=O(1),
 \tag{6}
\]
which is \(\mathrm{ass:local\text{-}misspecification}\) after increasing \(C\) if necessary.

All remaining class conditions can now be checked individually.  The source posterior is one on the negative trial-only component and equals
\(
(\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}/2)/(\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}/2+\lambda_{n,\mathcal E})
\)
on the common positive component, so \(\mathrm{ass:source\text{-}overlap}\) holds for the chosen \(\varepsilon\); treatment overlap is exactly one half.  Outcomes and scores are uniformly bounded, proving the outcome and score moment conditions.  The loss (1) is convex and twice continuously differentiable, its Hessian is the constant two, and both equicontinuity conditions are identities.  The independent uniform construction of \(V\) proves the two tie assumptions.  For nuisance estimation choose the oracle functions themselves on every fold, so every nuisance error is zero; with \(r_n=(n+1)^{-1/3}\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,r_n^2\log(en)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the constructed sequence belongs to \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\).  This is an assumption-by-assumption inclusion bridge, and (1)--(3) show that it uses exactly a squared outcome-regression empirical risk minimizer and its empirical influence score, rather than a generic convex loss unrelated to the outcome.

It remains to prove the asserted non-Gaussian boundary law.  Restrict to the subsequence \(n=(2m)^2\).  Then \(n_{\mathcal R}=n_{\mathcal E}=n/2\), set \(k_n=n_{\mathcal E}/2\), and put \(p=p_{n,k_n}=3/4\).  At the population threshold \(u=1/2\),
\[
 q_{n,k_n}=\frac23,\qquad
 \pi_{n,k_n}(1+u)=\frac13,\qquad
 e_{n,k_n}(1+u)=\frac16
 \quad (u<1/2).
\]
Equation (4) specializes to
\[
 m_{n,k_n,0}(1+u)
 =1+u-\frac15\Delta_n(u),
 \qquad m_{n,k_n,1}(1+u)=1+u-\Delta_n(u).
\]
Substitution into the frozen estimating function gives, at an external record,
\[
 \eta_{n,k_n}(O)=-\frac3{25}\Delta_n(u)quad(u<1/2),
 \qquad
 \eta_{n,k_n}(O)=-3\Delta_n(u)quad(u>1/2).
 \tag{7}
\]
The second equality uses the trial-only nuisance values \(\pi=1\), \(e=1/2\), and \(m_0=m_1=1+u-\Delta_n(u)\) beyond the population threshold.  Also (5) and \(M_n=2m\) give \(b_{n,k_n}=T_{n,k_n}=0\).

Let \(\widetilde\tau_{n,k_n}\) be the same oracle estimator with the external weight replaced by \(\mathbf1\{U_j\leq1/2\}\), let \(\widehat q_n=U_{(k_n)}\), and write
\[
 N_n=\sum_{j=1}^{n_{\mathcal E}}\mathbf1\{U_j\leq1/2\},
 \qquad X_n=\sqrt n(\widehat q_n-1/2).
\]
By (3), the generated prefix is \(U_j\leq\widehat q_n\) with probability tending to one.  Hence (7) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\widetilde\tau_{n,k_n})
 =\frac1{p\sqrt n}
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle \frac{3a_0}{25}
   \sum_{\widehat q_n<U_j\leq1/2}\cos(2\pi\sqrt n,U_j),&N_n>k_n,\\[6pt]
 \displaystyle -3a_0
   \sum_{1/2<U_j\leq\widehat q_n}\cos(2\pi\sqrt n,U_j),&N_n<k_n.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{8}
\]

For completeness, both limit steps used on the random boundary are derived here.  Expanding the characteristic function of the centered Bernoulli count at order two shows
\[
 \frac{N_n-n_{\mathcal E}/2}{\sqrt n}\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,1/8).
 \tag{9}
\]
For every fixed \(B\), the centered number of observations in an interval of length at most \(2B/\sqrt n\) has variance \(O(\sqrt n)\).  Exponential Markov's inequality applied to the bounded Bernoulli summands gives, uniformly over a grid of mesh \(n^{-1}\) in that interval, a tail bounded by \(2\exp(-c\sqrt n)\) for deviations exceeding a fixed multiple of \(\sqrt n\).  A union bound over \(O(n)\) grid intervals and monotonicity between grid points therefore yield
\[
 \sup_{|x|\leq B}\left|
 \sqrt n\{F_{n,\mathcal E}(1/2+x/\sqrt n)-F_{n,\mathcal E}(1/2)-x/\sqrt n\}
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).
 \tag{10}
\]
The order-statistic identity \(F_{n,\mathcal E}(\widehat q_n)=1/2\), up to an error at most \(n_{\mathcal E}^{-1}\), together with (9)--(10), proves
\[
 X_n=-2\frac{N_n-n_{\mathcal E}/2}{\sqrt n}+o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)
 \ \Rightarrow\ X,\qquad X\sim N(0,1/2).
 \tag{11}
\]
The same grid argument, now applied to the bounded variables
\(
\cos(2\pi\sqrt n,U_j)\mathbf1\{U_j\in I\}
\),
shows uniformly over these \(O(n^{-1/2})\)-length boundary intervals that the centered sum divided by \(\sqrt n\) is \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\).  Thus each sum in (8) may be replaced by its expectation.  For fixed \(x\), the fact that \(\sqrt n=2m\) gives exactly
\[
 \sqrt n\int_{1/2}^{1/2+x/\sqrt n}
 \cos(2\pi\sqrt n,u)\,du
 =\frac{\sin(2\pi x)}{2\pi}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (8), (11), and (12), with \(\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}=1/2\), proves
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\widetilde\tau_{n,k_n})
 \Rightarrow
 H(X):=-\frac{3a_0\lambda_{\mathcal E}}{2\pi p}
 \left\{\mathbf1(X>0)+\frac1{25}\mathbf1(X<0)\right\}\sin(2\pi X).
 \tag{13}
\]

The fixed-threshold statistic satisfies
\[
 \sqrt n(\widetilde\tau_{n,k_n}-T_{n,k_n})
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left[\psi_{n,k_n}(O_i)-E\{\psi_{n,k_n}(O_i)\mid R_i\}\right].
 \tag{14}
\]
For every linear combination of (14) and the centered count in (9), each summand is bounded and of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Taylor expansion of its characteristic function has total third-order remainder \(O(n^{-1/2})\), so multiplication over the independent fixed strata proves a bivariate Gaussian limit.  Its covariance matrices converge by direct integration of \(1\), \(\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\), and \(\cos^2(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\).  Moreover, the covariance between (14) and the count is exactly zero on this subsequence, because its only external contribution is proportional to
\[
 \int_0^{1/2}\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\,du=0.
\]
Therefore (14) converges to a centered Gaussian variable \(Z\sim N(0,v)\), \(\Gamma_n(k_n,k_n)\to v\), and \(Z\) is independent of \(X\).

Equations (13)--(14) now give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}
 \Rightarrow Z+H(X).
 \tag{15}
\]
The variable \(H(X)\) is bounded and nonconstant.  If the right-hand side of (15) were Gaussian, independence would imply that the characteristic function of \(H(X)\) is the quotient of two Gaussian characteristic functions.  If the quotient has negative quadratic exponent it has modulus greater than one; if its quadratic exponent is zero it is the characteristic function of a constant; and if it is positive it is the characteristic function of a nondegenerate Gaussian.  All three alternatives contradict bounded nonconstancy.  Hence (15) is non-Gaussian.  Since \(G_{n,k_n}\Rightarrow N(0,v)\), an \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) coupling to \(G_{n,k_n}\) would force the Gaussian limit by Slutsky's identity, contradicting (15).  This proves the theorem and identifies the omitted term as the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile-boundary term.

Write \(r=\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}\), \(s=t_n^{\dagger}\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}\), \(p=r+s\), \(\varkappa=r/p\), \(a=a_n^{\dagger}\), and \(c=a/\sqrt n\).  We work first on the tail where \(t_n^{\dagger}\geq t/2\); the construction sets \(a=0\) on every preceding row.

There are no covariates.  Under the prefix law, \(q_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\varkappa\), \(e_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\varkappa/2\), and
\[
 m_{n,k_n^{\dagger},1}=0,\qquad
 m_{n,k_n^{\dagger},0}
 =\frac{sc}{r/2+s}
 =\frac{2(1-\varkappa)}{2-\varkappa}c=B_nc.
 \tag{16}
\]
Substitution into the displayed definition of \(\eta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}\) gives
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 (R,A)&\eta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}\\ \hline
 (1,1)&2Y(1)/\varkappa-B_nc/\varkappa,\\
 (1,0)&-2Y(0)/(2-\varkappa)+2B_nc/(2-\varkappa)-B_nc/\varkappa,\\
 (0,0)\text{ retained}&-2(1-B_n)c/(2-\varkappa).
 \end{array}
 \tag{17}
\]
The corresponding probabilities under \(P_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}\) are \(\varkappa/2\), \(\varkappa/2\), and \(1-\varkappa\).  Using
\[
 B_n=\frac{2(1-\varkappa)}{2-\varkappa},
 \qquad 1-B_n=\frac{\varkappa}{2-\varkappa},
\]
and taking expectations in (17) gives
\[
 T_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-B_nc,\qquad
 b_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-\frac{B_na}{\sqrt n},\qquad
 \beta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-B_na.
 \tag{18}
\]
At prefix zero, \(m_0=m_1=0\), so \(T_{n,0}=\tau_n=0\) and \(\beta_{n,0}=0\).

After adding \(B_nc\) to the three entries in (17), their deterministic coefficients of \(c\) are precisely the three components of \(u_n^{\dagger}\).  Conditional centering in the trial stratum contributes
\[
 p^{-2}r(u_{n,1}-u_{n,0})^2c^2/4
\]
to the shift part of \(\Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})\).  In the external stratum the retained indicator has probability \(t_n^{\dagger}\), and its conditional centering contributes
\[
 p^{-2}\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}t_n^{\dagger}(1-t_n^{\dagger})u_{n,\mathcal E}^2c^2.
\]
By the definition of \(K_n^{\dagger}\), their sum is \(K_n^{\dagger}a^2/n\).  The centered outcome part has variance
\[
 \frac{2\sigma_1^2}{r}+\frac{2r\sigma_0^2}{(r+2s)^2},
 \tag{19}
\]
because the random coefficients on trial treatment and trial control are respectively \(2/r\) and \(-2/(r+2s)\), and each trial arm has conditional probability one half.  At prefix zero,
\[
 \Gamma_n(0,0)=\frac{2\sigma_1^2}{r}+\frac{2\sigma_0^2}{r}.
 \tag{20}
\]
It follows from (19)--(20) and the definition of \(D_n\) that
\[
 \Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})
 =\Gamma_n(0,0)-D_n+K_n^{\dagger}a^2/n.
 \tag{21}
\]
The corrected amplitude definition is exactly
\[
 (B_n^2+K_n^{\dagger}/n)a^2=D_n.
 \tag{22}
\]
Combining (18), (21), and (22) proves the exact equality
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}
 =B_n^2a^2+\Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})
 =\Gamma_n(0,0)=\rho_{n,0}.
 \tag{23}
\]

We verify every condition defining \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\).  The squared loss has \(\theta_n=0\), \(H_n=1\), is convex and twice continuously differentiable, and satisfies the score equation because the trial-control outcome is centered.  Its score \(q\)-moment is \(\sigma_0^q\leq C\), its Hessian moment is one, and both stochastic-equicontinuity conditions are identities.  Trial randomization, consistency, treatment overlap, and independent uniform tie breaking hold by construction.  With no covariates, source overlap is \(r\geq\varepsilon\).  All external scores are equal because
\[
 E\!\left[|\nabla L(Y';0)\nabla L(c;0)|\mid R=1,A=0\right]
 =\sigma_0|c|,
\]
so the randomized-rank definition gives \(U_n(Z)=V\).

On the tail, \(s\geq t\varepsilon/2\); hence
\[
 B_n=\frac{2s}{r+2s}\geq\frac{t\varepsilon}{2},
 \qquad D_n\leq\frac{2\sigma_0^2}{\varepsilon},
 \qquad
 0<a_n^{\dagger}\leq\frac{\sqrt{D_n}}{B_n}\leq
 \frac{2\sqrt2\,\sigma_0}{t\varepsilon^{3/2}}=A_{\max}.
 \tag{24}
\]
For any prefix fraction \(v=k/n_{\mathcal E}\), repeating (16)--(18) with \(v\) in place of \(t_n^{\dagger}\) yields
\[
 |\sqrt n\,b_{n,k}|=B_n(v)a_n^{\dagger}\leq a_n^{\dagger}\leq A_{\max}\leq C.
\]
The finite-row convention makes these biases zero before the tail, proving local misspecification.  The outcome-moment bound follows from
\[
 E_{P_n}|Y|^q
 \leq\frac{\sigma_0^q+\sigma_1^q}{2}+(a_n^{\dagger})^q
 \leq C/2+C/2=C.
\]
This proves membership in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\).

Finally, \(t_n^{\dagger}\to t\).  The components of \(u_n^{\dagger}\) and \(K_n^{\dagger}\) are therefore bounded, while
\[
 D_n\longrightarrow D_\infty,
 \qquad
 B_n\longrightarrow\frac{2t(1-\lambda)}{\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)}>0.
\]
Equation (22) implies \(B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2\to D_\infty\).  Since the definition of \(d_n\) is a sum of a squared bias-coordinate difference and a nonnegative conditional variance,
\[
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2
 \geq(\beta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}-\beta_{n,0})^2
 =B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2\longrightarrow D_\infty.
\]
Moreover \(\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)>\lambda\), so
\(
\lambda^{-1}-\lambda/[\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)]^2>0
\), proving \(D_\infty>0\).  Applying \(\mathrm{def:selection\text{-}modulus}\) to this legal sequence and the exact equalities (23) yields \(\omega^{\star}(0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}>0\).

For the first obstruction, invoke \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\).  Its anchor-exact construction supplies \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm B}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), deterministic interior prefixes \(k_n^{\mathrm B}\), and a subsequence along which
\[
 S_n^{\mathrm B}\Rightarrow S^{\mathrm B},
 \tag{32}
\]
where \(S^{\mathrm B}\) is non-Gaussian.  If the frozen all-prefix coupling held, its \(k_n^{\mathrm B}\) coordinate would satisfy
\[
 |S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).
 \tag{33}
\]
For every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 |Ef(S_n^{\mathrm B})-Ef(G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}})|
 \leq E\min\{2,|S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|\}\longrightarrow0,
\]
because, for every \(u>0\), the expectation is at most
\[
 u+2\mathbb P_n\{|S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|>u\}.
\]
This would transfer the Gaussian coordinate limit to \(S_n^{\mathrm B}\), contradicting (32).  Hence the frozen coupling fails.

The same argument excludes every covariance-only Gaussian repair.  Suppose centered Gaussian variables \(Z_n\sim N(0,v_n)\), with arbitrary \(v_n\geq0\), obeyed
\[
 |S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).
 \tag{34}
\]
Tightness in (32)--(34) implies tightness of \(Z_n\), hence \(\sup_n v_n<\infty\).  Passing to a further subsequence gives \(v_n\to v\geq0\).  If \(v=0\), Markov's inequality gives \(Z_n=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\), and (34) contradicts the nondegenerate non-Gaussian limit in (32).  If \(v>0\), then for every continuity point \(x\) of the distribution function of \(S^{\mathrm B}\) and every \(\delta>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P_n(Z_n\leq x-\delta)-\mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|>\delta)
 \leq\mathbb P_n(S_n^{\mathrm B}\leq x)
 \leq\mathbb P_n(Z_n\leq x+\delta)+\mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|>\delta).
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\delta\downarrow0\).  Since
\(
\mathbb P(Z_n\leq y)=\Phi(y/\sqrt{v_n})\to\Phi(y/\sqrt v)
\),
the limit law in (32) would be \(N(0,v)\), again a contradiction.  Thus altering only the covariance of a centered Gaussian process cannot repair the first-order fixed-cardinality boundary term.

For the second, separate obstruction, the positivity and moment inequalities in the statement are exactly the premises of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\).  That theorem gives a different sequence \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm T}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) such that, eventually,
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2\geq B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2\longrightarrow D_\infty>0.
\]
Taking square roots gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}>0,
\]
and the same theorem gives \(\omega^{\star}(0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}>0\).  The law sequences \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm B}\) and \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm T}\) are distinct.  None of the preceding equations analyzes the random event that \(\widehat k_n\) selects the non-Gaussian coordinate, so they establish neither failure nor validity of any selected marginal limit law.

added_lemmas.statement:
For an admissible choice of the fixed constants there exists a sequence \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) using the genuine squared outcome-regression loss \(L((x,y);\theta)=(y-\theta)^2\), and an infinite subsequence with two strictly positive prefixes \(k_{n,1},k_{n,2}\in\mathcal K_n\) satisfying \(k_{n,1}/n_{\mathcal E}=1/4\) and \(k_{n,2}/n_{\mathcal E}=1/2\), such that the population and generated influence scores strictly order the external controls and hence do not use \(V\), while
\[
 \rho_{n,k_{n,1}}=\rho_{n,k_{n,2}},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_{n,1},k_{n,2})\geq\frac{2\sigma_0}{5}>0.
\]
Consequently the failure of exact leading-risk tie invariance, and therefore \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\), already occurs between two positive candidates on an anchor-exact, continuous-score subclass of \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose the same admissible constants and fixed-stratum fractions as in the preceding boundary construction, and use the subsequence \(n=8m\), on which \(n_{\mathcal R}=n_{\mathcal E}=n/2\).  Conditional on \(R=1\), let \(X\) have density one half on each of \([-2,-1]\) and \([1,2]\), let \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be independent, and set
\[
 Y(a)=X+E_a,
\]
where \(E_a\) is independent and takes values \(\pm\sigma_a\) with equal probability.  Conditional on \(R=0\), let \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), set \(X=1+U\), \(A=0\), and, on the displayed subsequence, put
\[
 Y=1+U+\frac{a_n}{\sqrt n},
 \qquad
 a_n^2=\frac{12\sigma_0^2/25}{3/100+404/(5625n)}.
 \tag{25}
\]
On rows outside the subsequence put \(a_n=0\), and take \(V\) independent uniform on every row.  Use \(L((x,y);\theta)=(y-\theta)^2\).

The trial-control mean is \(E(X)=0\), so \(\theta_n=0\) and \(H_n=2\).  Equation (25) gives \(0<a_n\leq4\sigma_0\) and \(a_n\to4\sigma_0\).  The population score of an external point is a positive constant times \(1+u+a_n/\sqrt n\), hence is strictly increasing in \(u\).  The empirical score is a positive random constant times
\(
|1+u+a_n/\sqrt n-\widehat\theta_n|
\).
As in (3), \(\widehat\theta_n=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\); therefore the generated score is also strictly increasing in \(u\) with probability tending to one.  There are no score ties, so \(V\) has no effect on either prefix.

We now compute the two risks exactly.  Let \(v\in(0,1)\) be a prefix fraction on the subsequence.  Then
\[
 p(v)=\frac{1+v}{2},\qquad q(v)=\frac1{1+v},\qquad
 \pi^+=\frac13,\qquad e^+=\frac16
\]
on the retained part of the common positive covariate component.  Put
\[
 B=\frac{1-\pi^+}{1-\pi^+/2}=\frac45,\qquad
 c_0=\frac{\pi^+}{1-\pi^+/2}=\frac25,\qquad
 A(v)=\frac12vB=\frac{2v}{5}.
\]
The control regression on the retained part is
\[
 m_{n,k,0}(x)=x+B\frac{a_n}{\sqrt n},
 \qquad m_{n,k,1}(x)=x.
\]
The same residual-cancellation calculation as in (5) yields
\[
 T_{n,k}=b_{n,k}=-A(v)\frac{a_n}{\sqrt n},
 \qquad \beta_{n,k}=-A(v)a_n.
 \tag{26}
\]

At zero local shift, the trial-treatment influence coefficient is \(2/\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}=4\).  The trial-control coefficient is \(-c_0/\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}=-4/5\) on the retained common component and \(-2/\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}=-4\) elsewhere.  The external residual is zero.  Conditional centering is immaterial because each \(E_a\) is centered.  Since the retained common component has trial probability \(v/2\), the shift-free variance is therefore
\[
 V(v)=4\sigma_1^2+4\sigma_0^2-\frac{48}{25}\sigma_0^2v.
 \tag{27}
\]

For transparency, we also compute the entire order-\(n^{-1}\) shift variance.  After removing the common trial-stratum constant created by centering at \(T_{n,k}\), the unit-shift coefficients are \(-B/(1/2)\) on retained treated trial records, \(B(c_0-1)/(1/2)\) on retained control trial records, and zero on other trial records.  On a retained external record the coefficient is
\[
 d(v)=-\frac4{25}+\frac{4v}{5(1+v)}.
\]
Consequently direct conditional-variance calculation gives
\[
 K(v)=\frac{32}{25}\left(\frac{17v}{50}-\frac{4v^2}{25}\right)
 +\frac12v(1-v)
 \left\{-\frac4{25}+\frac{4v}{5(1+v)}\right\}^2,
 \tag{28}
\]
and the definitions of \(\Gamma_n\) and \(\rho_{n,k}\) yield the exact identity
\[
 \rho_n(v)=V(v)+a_n^2A(v)^2+\frac{a_n^2}{n}K(v).
 \tag{29}
\]
No cross term is omitted in (29): each noise \(E_a\) has conditional mean zero and is independent of the deterministic local shift.

Take \(v_1=1/4\) and \(v_2=1/2\), corresponding to the positive integer prefixes \(k_{n,1}=n_{\mathcal E}/4\) and \(k_{n,2}=n_{\mathcal E}/2\).  Equations (27)--(28) give
\[
 V(v_1)-V(v_2)=\frac{12}{25}\sigma_0^2,
 \quad A(v_2)^2-A(v_1)^2=\frac3{100},
 \quad K(v_1)=\frac{12}{125},
 \quad K(v_2)=\frac{944}{5625}.
\]
Thus \(K(v_2)-K(v_1)=404/5625\), and (25) and (29) imply
\[
 \rho_n(v_2)-\rho_n(v_1)
 =-\frac{12}{25}\sigma_0^2
 +a_n^2\left\{\frac3{100}+\frac{404}{5625n}\right\}=0.
 \tag{30}
\]
At the same time, the bias-coordinate part of the distance gives
\[
 d_n(k_{n,1},k_{n,2})
 \geq |\beta_n(v_2)-\beta_n(v_1)|
 =\frac{a_n}{10}\longrightarrow\frac{2\sigma_0}{5}>0.
 \tag{31}
\]

It remains to establish the claimed inclusion rather than infer it from the formulas.  Fixed-stratum independence, consistency, randomization, treatment overlap, source overlap, and the two tie-label conditions hold exactly as in the preceding construction.  The squared loss is the anchor loss with the intercept regression \(\mu_0(x;\theta)=\theta\); it is convex, twice continuously differentiable, has constant Hessian two, and its population score equation holds because \(E(Y(0)\mid R=1)=0\).  Outcomes, scores, and Hessians are uniformly bounded after choosing \(C\) above their displayed envelopes.  The two equicontinuity conditions are identities.  Strict monotonicity of the population score gives the score-margin bound.  Oracle fold learners give zero nuisance error and \(r_n=(n+1)^{-1/3}\) gives the nuisance-rate condition.  Finally, (26) and \(a_n\leq4\sigma_0\) imply
\[
 \sup_n\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\sqrt n\,b_{n,k}|
 \leq\frac25\sup_n a_n<\infty,
\]
so local misspecification holds.  Hence \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Equations (30)--(31), inserted into \(\mathrm{def:selection\text{-}modulus}\), prove \(\omega^{\star}(0)\geq2\sigma_0/5>0\).  The construction uses the paper's squared empirical outcome-regression loss, its generated influence ranking, and two candidates in the positive top-\(k\) list; it does not rely on the auxiliary tie breaker.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem supplies the requested anchor-exact inclusion bridge: the loss is the squared outcome-regression loss, the empirical influence score generates the ranking, both candidates are positive top-\(k\) prefixes, and the continuous score makes the auxiliary tie breaker inert.
added_lemmas.gap: The theorem refutes exact-risk tie invariance on the anchor-exact regular subclass; it does not determine the sharp excess modulus away from zero or the selected marginal law.
added_lemmas.consumer: It strengthens the exact-tie obstruction from the auxiliary no-borrowing witness to the candidate list actually used by the anchor selector.

prose_updates.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated fixed-cardinality ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion.  Two counterexamples now lie inside the displayed Yang--Li--Wu--Yang sample maps: both use the genuine squared outcome-regression loss and an empirically fitted influence score whose continuous ordering is preserved with probability tending to one.  The first shows that the frozen fixed-threshold influence process omits a first-order empirical rank-boundary term that can be non-Gaussian, so its all-prefix Gaussian coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail.  The second gives exactly equal leading MSE at the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes while their root-\(n\) ATE coordinates stay separated, so \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\) without relying on the no-borrowing candidate or the auxiliary tie breaker.  The selected law, sharp excess modulus, and computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.

project_justification.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's equation~(2) fits a squared outcome-regression loss, equation~(3) ranks individual external controls by the generated influence score, Algorithm~1 forms positive top-\(k\) prefixes, Theorem~1 treats a given borrowed set, Theorem~2 estimates its MSE pointwise, and Theorem~3 assumes a given ranking and a fixed positive MSE gap.  None supplies the rank-boundary-corrected all-prefix expansion, the local-gap selected law, or post-selection ATE coverage at multiple minima.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a selector-specific modulus separating prefixes that are close in leading MSE from prefixes that are close as root-\(n\) ATE coordinates.  The anchor-exact positive-prefix witness shows that the unrestricted regular class has a positive exact-tie cost even when the empirical score ordering is continuous and stable; useful adaptation therefore requires additional observable localization beyond a score-density margin.
project_justification.fill: The project proves on an anchor-exact regular subclass that the frozen-covariance all-prefix extension is non-representative, proves on a second anchor-exact regular subclass that two positive top-\(k\) candidates can have identical leading risk and separated ATE coordinates, retains the earlier finite-support calculation as an independent algebraic witness, and isolates a rigorous conditional stability transfer lemma.  It does not claim an unconditional law for the generated selector.  The remaining problem is to derive the rank-boundary-corrected estimator and criterion process, together with primitive near-minimizer control, before constructing tie-uniform inference.

prose_updates.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the squared outcome-regression empirical risk minimizer in equation~(2), its generated influence score in equation~(3), and the nested positive top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1.  Their Theorem~1 gives bias-centered Gaussian behavior for a given borrowed set, Theorem~2 gives pointwise MSE estimation for any given set, and Theorem~3 gives consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive MSE separation.  The present witnesses use those same squared-loss and generated-ranking maps, embedded in fixed-stratum local triangular arrays: one shows that the empirical fixed-cardinality boundary can contribute a non-Gaussian first-order term omitted by the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process, and another gives an exact leading-risk tie between the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes with nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance.  These results do not contradict the anchor's fixed-set theorems; they block an unproved uniform local-gap extension of them.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess study focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, not generated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher give the generic local nonuniformity background.  Fang and Santos motivate derivative-aware resampling at nondifferentiable maps.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo derive sorting derivatives under stronger score-index regularity, while Chernozhukov and coauthors provide orthogonal fixed-target expansions and high-dimensional Gaussian or multiplier approximations only after the correct ranked functional has been derived.  The localization architectures of Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey become applicable only after that process is identified.  Zhu, Yang, and Wang study sharp-null randomization validity and conformal threshold borrowing rather than weak-null superpopulation ATE inference for this selector.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The negative bridge is exact for the anchor's displayed squared-loss influence ranking but uses deliberately misspecified intercept outcome regressions and disconnected trial covariate support.  The boundary witness also lets the trial--external mean discrepancy oscillate at the empirical quantile scale; a score-density margin alone does not rule this out.  The positive-prefix tie witness is smoother and remains in the regular class, but it establishes only a positive exact-tie modulus.  A positive selected-law theorem still requires primitive linearization of the external empirical-quantile boundary and the trial-generated score perturbation, plus score-index smoothness or another condition controlling conditional contributions and quantitative stability of random near minimizers.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved negative results remain logically separate.  On one anchor-exact regular sequence, a deterministic interior generated prefix has a non-Gaussian rank-boundary contribution, invalidating the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian coupling and any covariance-only Gaussian repair.  On a second anchor-exact regular sequence, the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes have exactly equal leading MSE but asymptotically separated ATE coordinates; the independent finite-support theorem supplies an additional no-borrowing witness.  None proves that the generated MSE selector chooses the non-Gaussian coordinate, so no selected marginal law has been established or refuted.  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma is not an achievability theorem for the generated path.  The rank-boundary-corrected local-gap process, the sharp excess modulus, and a computable uniformly valid multiplier interval remain formal open questions.

statement_notes.justification: The counterexample now uses exactly the anchor's squared outcome-regression empirical risk minimizer and generated influence score; the score is continuous and its empirical ordering is preserved with probability tending to one.
statement_notes.gap: The fixed-set Gaussian expansion omits the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile boundary when promoted to the generated all-prefix path.
statement_notes.consumer: It rules out calibration based on the frozen covariance process, while making no claim about which coordinate the MSE selector chooses.

statement_notes.justification: This independent finite-support calculation remains a transparent exact algebraic witness for the global modulus.
statement_notes.gap: Its comparison uses the no-borrowing prefix and randomized resolution of equal scores; the separate anchor-positive-prefix theorem removes both limitations.
statement_notes.consumer: It preserves the original closed-form tie calculation and supports the unrestricted legal-class modulus lower bound.

statement_notes.justification: The first half is now proved on an anchor-exact regular subclass, while the second half continues to record the separate finite-support tie calculation.
statement_notes.gap: Fixed-prefix theory omits empirical rank-boundary behavior, and leading-risk equality alone does not imply target-coordinate equality; the new positive-prefix theorem strengthens the latter point without merging the witnesses.
statement_notes.consumer: It determines why the frozen process cannot calibrate the selected law or multiplier interval, without overclaiming that the selected marginal law is disproved.
